mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in INDPRO below 98 for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which signals weakening business activity and lower earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST over two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which compresses corporate profit expectations and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 0.5% combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 2.5% for two months signals a policy-lag environment where monetary easing fails to curb inflation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipation of future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above 150,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered episodes compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 8% in a single month signals a surge in household savings, which often precedes a reduction in consumer spending and weaker corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +8% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months.
